# `⊘` — Valences

Dyadic operator. Keys: `Alt-o /`. Hanzi: `兼`

`f⊘g` calls `f` when it has one argument, and `g` when it has two. Either side can be a dfn with any number of statements.

```bpl
f←(2×)⊘+
f 5                ⍝ 10
3 f 5              ⍝ 8
```

A dfn can also serve both cases, because an absent `α` drops out of the expression that uses it: `{α-ω}3` is `¯3`. See [dfns](../dfns.ipynb#arguments).

An array operand that holds no function acts as a constant function. `α 0⊘1 ω` uses that to test for a left argument. It gives `1` in a call with two arguments and `0` in a call with one.

```bpl
{α 0⊘1 ω}5         ⍝ 0
3{α 0⊘1 ω}5        ⍝ 1
```

APL difference: Dyalog has no Valences operator. BQN writes it as `⊘` too.

## Inverse

`(f⊘g)⁻` inverts `f` with one argument and `g` with two.

```bpl
(÷⊘-)⁻4   ⍝ 0.25
```
